name: The Stillwater Purge: 2197 Shelf Fire Was Deliberate
description: The Stillwater District fire of 2197 is officially recorded as an industrial accident — a cascade failure in a recycled-fuel processing plant that burned 14 blocks of Shelf housing and killed an estimated 2,300 residents. But survivors, historians, and Shelf community organizers have long maintained that the fire was deliberately set to clear the Stillwater corridor for the Helios-Vantage corponation's subsequent infrastructure expansion, which broke ground exactly 11 months after the blaze. A 2214 investigative series by independent journalist Kwame Osei-Okonkwo-Ibáñez, published across six Underworld nodes before being legally suppressed, presented fire pattern analysis suggesting four simultaneous ignition points.
cultural_impact: The Stillwater fire is commemorated annually on March 14th in the Shelf with unregistered candlelight gatherings that corponation security routinely disperses — the dispersion itself becoming a recurring flashpoint. 'Stillwater' is used as shorthand in Shelf communities for any situation where corporate expansion follows community destruction with suspicious convenience.
key_figures: Journalist Kwame Osei-Okonkwo-Ibáñez (in exile, Underworld-only presence since 2215)
Stillwater Survivors Collective founder Deshawn Mukherjee-Castillo
locations: Former Stillwater District (now Helios-Vantage Transit Hub, Tier 2 boundary)
Shelf memorial site 'The Char' — unmarked, maintained by community
story_hooks: A player discovers their family lost someone in the Stillwater fire — and a recently unearthed piece of chromework recovered from the rubble contains data that shouldn't exist
Deshawn Mukherjee-Castillo asks the players to protect Kwame Osei-Okonkwo-Ibáñez during a planned return to GLMZ to testify before a citizen tribunal — Helios-Vantage is aware of the plan

A Helios-Vantage whistleblower from the infrastructure division makes contact with the players, carrying a 2196 internal document that predates the fire — a land acquisition proposal for the Stillwater corridor
believers: Shelf residents, survivors and descendants, anti-corporate activists, independent historians, Underworld researchers
evidence: Osei-Okonkwo-Ibáñez's fire pattern analysis is accurate; internal Helios-Vantage documents confirming foreknowledge exist in the Underworld archive but have been subject to continuous legal suppression and authenticity challenges funded by Helios-Vantage's legal division
